rendered:
NFA-A: after the C-rate was lowered from 1C[1] back to 0.1C[2], it recovered ≈170 mAh g^− 1[3], against an initial 0.1C[4] capacity (before the rate tests) of ≈184 mAh g^− 1[5]. The paper describes this as similar (≈5%)[6] to the initial value, i.e. a loss of about that amount. The stated figures themselves imply a somewhat larger drop than that approximate figure.

NFA-F: it recovered only ≈138 mAh g^− 1[7], against an initial 0.1C[8] capacity of ≈190 mAh g^− 1[9], which the paper reports as a ≈27% loss[10].

The paper concludes from this that NFA-A was the most stable of the variants under these test conditions, compared with NFA 811[11] and NFA-F.
